item.title: France’s Economy Is Trapped in a Negative Feedback Loop
item.content:encoded: The French government desperately needs a return to strong growth if it is to contain its rapidly rising debts.

item.title: U.S. Home Price Growth Increases Again
item.content:encoded: The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller National Home Price Index, which measures home prices across the country, rose 1.9% in the 12 months through July, compared with a 1.6% increase in June.

item.title: Average 30-year mortgage rates hit 7.03% this week, the first time they have surpassed 7% since the beginning of last year
item.content:encoded: The effect of rates topping the psychologically important 7% level is rippling through the market for buyers, sellers and builders.

item.title: KB Home Cuts Margin Outlook as Housing Conditions Worsen
item.content:encoded: The homebuilder said it now expects annual gross profit margin to be 16.0% to 16.2%, down from its earlier guidance of 16.1% to 16.5%.

item.title: Many people who are willing to move a little further from the city, or buy a smaller home, are figuring out that it is still possible to buy
item.content:encoded: A tour of a neighborhood near Seattle shows how a younger generation is making it work in one of the least affordable housing markets in decades.

item.title: After Kevin Warsh took over the Fed this spring, he said he wanted investors to watch the economy, not the Fed: Play the ball, not the referee. Last week, the referees stepped in
item.content:encoded: Kevin Warsh wants investors to focus on the economy and not the Fed. Last week, his top lieutenants stepped in to reset bets on an October rate increase.

item.title: What Six Years of Inflation Mean for the Midterms
item.content:encoded: Inflation is cooler than it was four years ago, but voters are still paying much higher prices.

item.title: U.S. consumer spending is on the rise despite frustrations with persistent inflation and gloomy views about the economy
item.content:encoded: Spending is rising because prices are climbing and Americans are buying more stuff.

item.title: Consumer Sentiment Ticked Lower in September
item.content:encoded: The University of Michigan survey’s headline index landed at 48.1 in September, down from 51.7 in August.

item.title: German Exports Fall Further, Clouding Picture of Resilience
item.content:encoded: The result points to volatility in international demand and dims hopes that trade will underpin the country’s economic growth this year.

item.title: President Trump has formed a committee to evaluate the mortgage-fraud allegations made against Fed governor Lisa Cook
item.content:encoded: The move signaled a renewed effort to fire the Biden-appointed Fed governor as part of the president’s desire to wield more control over the central bank.

item.title: Canada Jobless Rate Edges Up With Another Drop in Employment
item.content:encoded: Employers in Canada cut 68,300 jobs in September, nudging the unemployment rate up 0.1 percentage point to 6.5%.

item.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: U.S. Inflation Data in Focus
item.content:encoded: Investors will be focused on inflation data from the U.S., eurozone and China as well as U.K. economic growth figures and trade data out of China.

item.title: The typical American family got a little wealthier in the years following the pandemic, while well-off and older Americans got much richer
item.content:encoded: A Federal Reserve study found overall median net worth rose 2% between 2022 and 2025.

item.title: Consumer Sentiment Drops, per Michigan Survey
item.content:encoded: The University of Michigan survey’s headline index fell to 46.3 in its preliminary October reading, versus 48.1 in September.

item.title: IMF Chief Tells Economic Leaders: The Time to Act Is Now
item.content:encoded: Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said the global economy is caught in a tug of war between an energy shock and an artificial-intelligence boom.

item.title: Global Economy Stronger Than Expected, But Threats Mount, OECD Says
item.content:encoded: A lengthy conflict in the Middle East in combination with other headwinds could take a big toll on activity around the world, the Paris-based research body said.

item.title: Eurozone Economy Surged as War Ignited Energy Prices
item.content:encoded: The bloc’s GDP picked up more rapidly than previously estimated in the quarter through June, but that resilience will be tested if the Iran war continues to block the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Mortgage rates posted their largest increase in four years this week
item.content:encoded: The rise to 7.28% follows the bond-market rout and deals another blow to a limping housing market.

item.title: India’s Central Bank Raises Rates For First Time Since 2023
item.content:encoded: The Reserve Bank of India raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years as the Middle East conflict keeps energy prices high, hurting the rupee and fueling inflation fears.
